These technical and organizational security measures shall ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including, as appropriate, (a) pseudonymisation and encryption;"},{"id":"p0681","text":"(b) the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services;"},{"id":"p0682","text":"(c) the ability to restore the availability and access to the Personally Identifiable Information in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident; and (d) a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of those measures."},{"id":"p0683","text":"11.4.4 Each Party shall notify the other Party of: (a) any unauthorized use or disclosure or breach of any Personally Identifiable Information promptly upon discovery of such occurrence; and (b) the transmittal of any related breach notification to any affected person, Governmental Authority or the media. input.quote: 15.15 Rights Reserved. No license or any other right is granted to either Party, by implication or otherwise, except as specifically set forth in this Agreement. All rights not exclusively granted to SFJ are reserved to PB and its Affiliates.
input.rationale: This funding agreement contains no vendor-to-customer licence grant to police: rather than licensing IP to us, SFJ leaves us in ownership. PB retains sole and exclusive ownership of all Existing PB Intellectual Property (11.1.1.1(a)), owns all Trial Inventions outright regardless of inventorship (11.1.1.3(a)), and acquires sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ, of the Trial Data Package and all Research Results (11.1.1.4); Section 15.15 reserves all rights not expressly granted to SFJ to "PB and its Affiliates". Ownership is broader than the preferred licence position — it is perpetual, cannot be revoked at SFJ's discretion (no "revocable" or at-will termination language appears anywhere), and is inherently exercisable by our affiliates and by contractors acting on our behalf. Section 15.6 also lets either Party assign, sublicense or transfer the Agreement and all of its rights to an Affiliate or to a successor "in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise", which satisfies the successor/M&A transfer element without any consent requirement. Third-party contractor rights are also directed to us on freely-assignable, multi-tier sublicensable terms (11.1.1.3(c)). The only structural point worth noting (not a deviation) is that SFJ holds the Trial Data Package until the purchase/assignment trigger, but the Research Results are deemed PB's Confidential Information with PB as disclosing Party, so our use is unrestricted in the interim. No redline is warranted; flagging this would only weaken a bargain that already benefits us.

input.summary: Limit the affiliate/successor assignment carve-out to PB, add a reasonableness standard to assignment consent, make the competitor-assignment bar permanent, and remove SFJ's termination right on a PB Change of Control.
input.comment: [Playbook] We keep our affiliate and successor assignment freedom but limit that carve-out to PB, so SFJ may assign only with our prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), and we extend the bar on SFJ assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor so it applies at all times. We also remove SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate on a PB Change of Control, together with the 150% payment and consequences that turned on that termination.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.",
  "Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.",
  "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.",
  "Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.",
  "Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.",
  "Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Both parties may assign to a successor.",
  "A successor assignment requires written notice.",
  "Other assignments require consent.",
  "Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld."
]

input.summary: Limit the affiliate/successor assignment carve-out to PB, add a reasonableness standard to assignment consent, make the competitor-assignment bar permanent, and delete SFJ's termination right on a PB Change of Control.
input.comment: [Playbook] We keep our affiliate and successor assignment freedom but limit that carve-out to PB, so SFJ may assign only with our prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), and we extend the bar on SFJ assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor beyond Program Transfer. We also delete Section 14.2.6, which let SFJ terminate in its sole discretion on a PB Change of Control; our playbook treats a change-of-control exit right as a walk-away.

input.quote: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.
input.rationale: Section 15.6 already gives PB the preferred assignment freedom (affiliate and successor/M&A transfers without consent), but the bargain fails the playbook on three points, one of which is walk-away territory. Section 14.2.6 lets SFJ terminate the entire Agreement in its sole discretion following a PB Change of Control (with a 150% Development Costs payment), which is an express vendor exit right on our change of control. Section 15.6 also extends the same consent-free affiliate/successor carve-out to SFJ (so SFJ can assign without our consent), and states no reasonableness standard for consent to other assignments. Section 15.6's bar on SFJ assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor expires at Program Transfer. We therefore target the preferred position: the affiliate/successor carve-out is limited to PB, consent is subject to a reasonableness standard, the competitor bar applies at all times (waivable only in PB's sole discretion), and SFJ's change-of-control termination right and its payment machinery are removed. The fallback level is not used because it would require deleting our own no-consent affiliate carve-out. We have left SFJ's limited-partner/liquidating-trust right to assign the receipt of Approval Payments (Section 15.6, final paragraph) untouched as a financing mechanic, and PB's Change of Control Buy-Out Option (6.7.2) is a right in our favour.

We also remove SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate on a PB Change of Control and its associated 150% payment, since a change-of-control exit right against us is a walk-away under our playbook.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary of the review (ASSIGN — deviation, preferred target):**

- **15.6 (p0814):** PB already has the preferred affiliate and successor/M&A carve-outs — those two elements are already met. But the carve-out runs to "either Party," so SFJ can also assign without our consent, and no reasonableness standard applies to consent. Cured by two surgical edits (carve-out limited to PB; consent "not to be unreasonably withheld").
- **15.6, competitor bar (p0817):** the prohibition on SFJ transferring to a pharma/biotech competitor expired at Program Transfer; now applies at all times, waivable only in PB's sole discretion.
- **14.2.6 (p0765–p0766):** walk-away term — SFJ could terminate in its sole discretion on a PB Change of Control, with a 150% Development Costs payment. Removed the termination right and conformed the stranded consequence paragraph so no dangling mechanic remains; the PB notice sentence is preserved verbatim.
- Left untouched as favourable/neutral to us: PB's Change of Control Buy-Out Option (6.7.2) and SFJ's limited-partner/liquidating-trust right to assign receipt of Approval Payments.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Verifier reasons:
- Preferred level is complete: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (PB-only affiliate/successor carve-out, mutual consent gate now binding SFJ, reasonableness standard, perpetual competitor bar, and an express "no right to terminate" on PB Change of Control).
- Fallback level is not complete (mutual successor right and written-notice mechanic are absent), but that is immaterial because the drafter targeted the preferred level, and the rationale correctly explains that using the fallback would surrender our existing consent-free affiliate carve-out.
- Minimality defect: the second sentence added to 14.2.6, "This Agreement shall continue in full force and effect following a Change of Control of PB.", is declaratory boilerplate that duplicates the operative effect of the immediately preceding "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB." No selected element requires it. Delete that sentence; the no-termination sentence alone carries the element.
- Otherwise the edits are tightly scoped: "either Party" narrowed to "PB", the reasonableness qualifier inserted, "prior to the date of Program Transfer" changed to "at any time" with its avoidance-of-doubt sunset removed, and the 14.2.6 termination right deleted. Deleting the 150% Development Costs payment and the p0766 consequences paragraph is proper rather than over-reach, since both were contingent solely on a termination under 14.2.6 that no longer exists; retaining them would have left dangling "such termination" references.
- Intent preserved: PB's Change of Control notice duty, PB's Buy-Out Option (6.7.2), and SFJ's limited-partner/liquidating-trust right to assign receipt of Approval Payments are untouched, and the "Notwithstanding any of the foregoing" opener keeps PB's sole-discretion competitor veto from conflicting with the new reasonableness standard. One drafting check before sending: confirm no other provision (e.g. effects-of-termination or Article 6 adjustment provisions) cross-references "Section 14.2.6" as a termination event, so the deletion leaves no dangling cross-reference.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

input.quote: NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES OR LOST OR IMPUTED PROFITS OR ROYALTIES OR COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES
input.rationale: Section 15.11 (p0833) is the only limitation-of-liability provision: it contains a mutual indirect/consequential damages waiver (already meeting that element) but no aggregate monetary cap. Article 12 (indemnification), the 13.6 disclaimer and 14.4.2 (which only channels SFJ's termination damages into the Section 14.2 payments) add no cap, and document-wide searches for \"aggregate liability\"/\"shall not exceed\" return nothing responsive, so both Parties' direct liability is unlimited and the rule fails. We cure at the preferred level: because Article 6 payments are event/approval-driven and a bare twelve-month lookback could compute to nil, the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor is needed to make the mutual cap real, which also completes the preferred formula together with the data protection/security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs. The basis is anchored to PB's Article 6 payments because this Co-Development Agreement has no \"fees\" concept, and the retained savings sentence is extended in place so all PB payment obligations are not \"damages\" subject to the cap. Nothing else in 15.11 is disturbed; the SFJ Article 4 funding carve-out proposed earlier has been dropped as outside the checklist.

proposal.summary: Add mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' Article 6 payments and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirm PB's payment obligations are not capped damages
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15.11 waives indirect damages but leaves both Parties' direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' Article 6 payments (this Agreement has no defined "fees") and USD 1,000,000, the floor being necessary because Article 6 payments are event-driven and could otherwise be nil. Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and PB's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to it.

Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and PB's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to it.

ops.text: Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12, each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10, each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations, each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and each Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000).

ops.oldText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2.
ops.newText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2, OR ANY OTHER PB PAYMENT OBLIGATION, WHICH ARE NOT "DAMAGES" SUBJECT TO ANY CAP.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.",
  "The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.",
  "The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.",
  "Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.",
  "Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.",
  "Indemnification obligations are uncapped.",
  "Gross negligence is uncapped.",
  "Wilful misconduct is uncapped.",
  "Fraud is uncapped.",
  "Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.",
  "Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.",
  "The cap is based on 12 months of fees.",
  "Indemnification obligations are uncapped.",
  "Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.",
  "Gross negligence is uncapped.",
  "Wilful misconduct is uncapped."
]

Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 15.11 (p0833) is the only limitation-of-liability provision in the Agreement. It gives a mutual waiver of indirect/consequential damages but contains **no aggregate monetary cap at all** — leaving PB's direct liability unlimited. Neither Article 12 (indemnification/insurance), the 13.6 disclaimer, nor 14.4.2 (exclusive remedy, which only channels SFJ's termination damages into the Section 14.2 payments) supplies a cap, and document-wide searches for "aggregate liability" / "shall not exceed" returned nothing responsive.

**Classification:** deviation — fails the fallback (mutual 12-month fees cap with carve-outs).

**Cure (fallback, one operation):** a new Section 15.11.1 imposing a mutual cap at fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carved out. I did not volunteer the preferred USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor or the additional preferred carve-outs, and the retained final sentence of 15.11 (preserving PB's Article 6 / 14.2 payment obligations) keeps the payment mechanics intact.

Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Fallback checklist is complete on the face of the inserted sentence: mutual aggregate cap, 12-month fee basis, and the four required carve-outs (Article 12 indemnities, Article 10 confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct).
- Preferred level fails on four elements: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, no data protection/security carve-out, no fraud carve-out, and no carve-out for infringement of the other Party's IP. The temporal anchor is also "preceding the claim" rather than "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" (acceptable at fallback, noted for the preferred formula).
- Minimality is satisfied: one appended sentence, no rewrite of 15.11, no deletion of the retained indirect-damages waiver, the deemed-consequential-damages sentence, or the PB Article 6/14.2 savings sentence; no survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories were added.
- Intent defect 1 — indeterminate cap basis. This Co-Development Agreement contains no "fees" concept or defined "Fees"; the consideration streams are Development Costs funded by SFJ and the Article 6 approval/contingent payments by PB. "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months" therefore has no resolvable referent and could compute to zero, making the mutual cap illusory (and, for SFJ's exposure to PB, worse than the current uncapped position and inside walk-away territory of "below 6 months' fees"). Repair: tie the basis to a defined stream, e.g. "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim" (or the greater of that amount and USD 1,000,000).
- Intent defect 2 — collision with SFJ's core funding mechanic. The new cap is drafted at large ("arising out of or relating to this Agreement") and, unlike PB's payments, nothing preserves SFJ's Article 5 obligation to fund Development Costs; a failure-to-fund claim by PB would now be capped by an amount that may be nil. Repair: extend the existing savings sentence, e.g. "...nor to limit either Party's obligation to pay the amounts set forth in Article 5, Article 6 or Section 14.2," or expressly carve debt/payment obligations out of the cap.
- Intent defect 3 — payment carve-out too narrow. The retained sentence excludes only Article 6 and Section 14.2 amounts from Section 15.11; all other PB payment obligations now sit inside the aggregate cap. State expressly that Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement are not "damages" subject to the cap.
- Drafting note for the redline comment: the comment is accurate and concise, but it should flag that "fees" is undefined here and propose the Article 6 anchor as the operative fix rather than relying on the generic model wording.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

input.quote: NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES OR LOST OR IMPUTED PROFITS OR ROYALTIES OR COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES
input.rationale: Section 15.11 (p0833) is the only limitation-of-liability provision: it contains a mutual indirect/consequential damages waiver (already meeting that element) but no aggregate monetary cap. Article 12 (indemnification), the 13.6 disclaimer and 14.4.2 (which only channels SFJ's termination damages into the Section 14.2 payments) add no cap, and document-wide searches for \"aggregate liability\"/\"shall not exceed\" return nothing responsive, so both Parties' direct liability is unlimited and the rule fails. We cure at the preferred level: because Article 6 payments are event/approval-driven and a bare twelve-month lookback could compute to nil, the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor is needed to make the mutual cap real, which also completes the preferred formula together with the data protection/security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs. The basis is anchored to PB's Article 6 payments because this Co-Development Agreement has no \"fees\" concept, and the retained savings sentence is extended in place so all PB payment obligations are not \"damages\" subject to the cap. Nothing else in 15.11 is disturbed; the SFJ Article 4 funding carve-out proposed earlier has been dropped as outside the checklist.

proposal.summary: Add mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' Article 6 payments and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirm PB's payment obligations are not capped damages
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15.11 waives indirect damages but leaves both Parties' direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' Article 6 payments (this Agreement has no defined "fees") and USD 1,000,000, the floor being necessary because Article 6 payments are event-driven and could otherwise be nil. Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and PB's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to it.

ops.text: Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12, each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10, each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations, each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and each Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000).

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.2 is PB's only convenience exit, but it fails the fallback on material terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, it closes entirely once the first Regulatory Approval is received, and the notice period is left blank ([***]) rather than set at 60-90 days. In a multi-year development term that is effectively no reliable customer convenience right. SFJ's exits (14.2.3 MAE, 14.2.5 bankruptcy, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.7 safety, 14.2.8.1 compliance breach, 14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, 14.2.10 JSC decision) are each trigger-based rather than at-will, so we have not treated them as vendor convenience rights; the redline confirms that position expressly. We targeted the preferred level because the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap has no analogue in this deal (the 300% Development Cost payment is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package, not a subscription penalty) and we have left that buy-out economics untouched. Notice period ambiguity and the retained 300% buy-out are noted commercially, not separately redlined.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: T4C — deviation (preferred-level redline at §14.2.2).**

- **What's wrong:** PB's only at-will exit (§14.2.2) is doubly gated — it opens only after SFJ has paid or incurred $60M of Development Costs and shuts on first Regulatory Approval — with a blank notice period. In a multi-year development term that fails even the fallback (no reliable 60–90 day customer convenience right).
- **SFJ's side:** every SFJ exit (MAE, bankruptcy, Change of Control, safety, compliance breach, Adverse Patent Impact, JSC deadlock) is trigger-based, not at-will, so I did not flag them as vendor convenience rights; the redline states that expressly to lock the position.
- **Cure (one surgical replace):** unconditional PB convenience termination on thirty (30) days' notice, pro rata refund of prepayments, and no SFJ convenience termination during the Term. The 300% Development Cost payment is left intact because it is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package rather than an early-termination penalty, and no fee-cap element sits at the preferred level.

Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Deterministic failures:
- Customer convenience termination present: failed

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (unconditional PB convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepayments, express bar on SFJ convenience termination during the Term). Nothing is left to the margin comment.
- The deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' flag (ok=false) is a false negative on substance: the clause names the customer as "PB" rather than a generic "Customer", and the operative grant "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice" is plainly present.
- Fallback is not met (30-day notice is outside the 60–90 day band and the retained 300% Development Cost buy-out is uncapped), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete; a level need only be satisfied at one tier.
- Minimality holds: only the two gating conditions ($60M spend threshold and the pre-first-Regulatory-Approval window) and the blank [***] notice figure were removed — each removal is necessary to make the convenience right unconditional and the notice period certain — and the two insertions map one-to-one to the refund and no-Vendor-convenience elements. The 300% buy-out, Approval Payment carry-over, Section 6.2 adjustment and credit language are retained verbatim, and no survival tail, expense language or procedure was added.
- Minor drafting note (not a minimality failure): the refund sentence reads "any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB" rather than "prepaid fees". The broadening is a reasonable adaptation because this agreement does not use "fees" as a defined payment concept (PB's payments are Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payment, etc.), so a fees-only refund would be inoperative here.
- Intent is preserved: the retained buy-out economics, ARTICLE 6 cross-references, Section 11.1.1.4 Trial Data Package purchase mechanic and Section 6.2 adjustment all continue to function; the sentence "if PB elects to continue development ... following such termination" remains coherent now that termination may occur after first Regulatory Approval. No dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created.
- Residual commercial exposure to flag to the client (correctly handled in the rationale rather than by a second redline): PB's exit still costs 300% of Development Costs plus continuing Approval Payments, so the exit is unconditional but not free; and SFJ's Section 14.2.10 JSC-disagreement right, while trigger-based, is close to discretionary in practice and may warrant separate negotiation if SFJ resists the new no-convenience sentence.

input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.2 is PB's only at-will exit, and it fails the fallback on material terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, it closes entirely once the first Regulatory Approval is received, and the notice figure is left blank ([***]) rather than set within the 60-90 day band. In a multi-year development term that is not a usable customer convenience right. The redline restores it as an express termination "for convenience, without cause, at any time" on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, adds a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments (broadened from "fees" because this Agreement uses Approval Payments and Buy-Out Payment rather than a defined fee concept), and states that SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term. SFJ's exits (14.2.3 MAE, 14.2.5 bankruptcy, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.7 safety, 14.2.8.1 compliance breach, 14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, 14.2.10 JSC decision) are each trigger-based rather than at-will, so we do not flag them as vendor convenience rights; the new sentence confirms that reading. We target the preferred level because the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap has no analogue here: the retained 300% Development Cost payment is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package under Section 11.1.1.4, not a subscription penalty, and we leave those economics and the ARTICLE 6 carry-over untouched. Residual commercial points for negotiation (noted, not redlined): the exit is unconditional but not free, and 14.2.10 is close to discretionary in practice.

proposal.summary: Give PB an express unconditional right to terminate for convenience/without cause on 30 days' written notice with pro rata refund of prepayments, and bar SFJ convenience termination during the Term.

We have made it an express termination for convenience without cause on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments, and confirmed SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term.

content.text:
**Finding: LICENSE — compliant (no redline proposed).**

The agreement contains no vendor-to-customer licence grant, because SFJ does not license IP to us at all — we hold ownership:

- **11.1.1.1(a)** — PB remains sole and exclusive owner of all Existing PB Intellectual Property and of PB IP arising independently.
- **11.1.1.3(a)** — PB is the exclusive and sole owner of all Trial Inventions regardless of inventorship, with SFJ assigning and causing its affiliates/Permitted Third Parties to assign.
- **11.1.1.4** — PB acquires sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ, of the Trial Data Package including all Research Results.
- **15.15** — all rights not exclusively granted to SFJ are reserved to "PB and its Affiliates"; no PB IP is licensed to SFJ except under the Program Transfer Agreement.
- **15.6** — either Party may assign, sublicense or transfer the Agreement and all rights to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger/stock/asset sale, satisfying the successor-transfer element without consent.

Nothing in the document is revocable at SFJ's discretion (the word "revocable" appears nowhere), and no clause excludes our affiliates or contractors. Ownership subsumes the preferred checklist, so the rule sits above the preferred position and should not be redlined. Noted only in the rationale (not as a deviation): SFJ holds the Trial Data Package until the purchase trigger, but Research Results are deemed PB's Confidential Information with PB as disclosing Party, so our interim use is unrestricted.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.
