elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: The revised Section 14.4.2 still requires PB (Customer) to pay a liquidated sum on termination — "the sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee not exceeding Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ during the three months preceding such termination". A capped fee is still a Customer-payable liquidated amount, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not reached; the 14.2.1/14.2.2/14.2.10 formulas (300%; Development Costs plus 25% p.a.) also remain in the text.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly recharacterises and confines the termination consideration: "the sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee ...". The alternative-characterisation phrase closes the purchase-consideration route in 14.2/11.1.1.4, so the only liquidated amount PB can owe on termination is the early-termination fee. Retained Approval Payments under 14.2.2/14.2.10 are contingent post-approval milestone consideration, not liquidated damages, and Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments are an elective prepayment, so neither displaces this element.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The fee is expressly capped: "an early-termination fee not exceeding Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ during the three months preceding such termination". The Agreement contains no periodic fee payable by PB pre-approval (Approval Payments are approval-contingent and the SFJ Interim Management Fee is a redacted lump sum), so Development Costs is the ascertainable running-spend analogue; the temporal anchor is exactly three months and is not exceeded.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: "[T]he sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee ... in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have", and the sentence opens "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary", which reaches the Section 14.2 formulas (300%, 150%, Development Costs plus 25%). No other liquidated or penalty mechanic payable by PB survives (Section 6.4 default interest is compensatory interest, Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments are elective).

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single edit to the Section 14.4.2 proviso converts every Section 14.2 termination payment into one early-termination fee, caps it at three months of Development Costs, and declares it the sole amount payable by PB whether framed as liquidated damages or as Trial Data Package consideration.

Preferred level is not reached and should not be claimed: a capped Customer-payable liquidated sum remains, and the 14.2.1/14.2.2/14.2.5.2/14.2.6/14.2.7/14.2.8.1/14.2.10 formulas are left in the text. Reaching preferred would require deleting each formula, which the rationale correctly identifies as a larger economic rewrite.

Minimal: one surgical replacement inside the existing proviso; the favourable retained language ("without prejudice to other remedies such Party may have at law or equity" and the "in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have" tail) is preserved, no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category is added, and the pre-existing "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" opener is reused rather than a new override being bolted on. The added phrase "whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package" is necessary, not surplus, because the Section 14.2 sums are framed as purchase consideration and would otherwise escape the cap.

Intent preserved: the Section 11.1.1.4 Trial Data Package purchase mechanic, the 14.2.2/14.2.10 credits for "the amount previously paid ... pursuant to this Section", the Section 6.2 adjustment, Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments and post-approval Approval Payments all continue to operate against the capped fee; no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles.

Residual drafting risk to tighten (not a level failure): the retained 14.2 sentences still read "PB will pay SFJ ... an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs". The cap depends on the opening "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" carrying through the proviso. If SFJ pushes back, add "Notwithstanding Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10" inside the proviso itself (or conform each formula) so the override is beyond argument.

Second point to watch: the cap base is SFJ's spend rather than fees paid by PB. Confirm the three-month Development Costs figure is verifiable (e.g., tie it to the invoiced/reported Development Costs for the three calendar months preceding the termination effective date) so the ceiling cannot be inflated by costs merely "incurred" but unbilled.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-c59579f4","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE","rationale":"Section 12.1.1 lists SFJ's indemnity heads (gross negligence/wilful misconduct, material breach, Protocol breach, AZ License breach, post-transfer injury and product liability) but contains no third-party intellectual-property indemnity anywhere in the Agreement. Conversely, Section 12.1.2(f) makes PB indemnify SFJ for infringement of Third Party Intellectual Property \"by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder\" — a one-way IP indemnity running to the counterparty, which is our walk-away position. The Article 12.2 procedure (notice, control of defence, cooperation) is already adequate and unchanged. We therefore target the fallback: an SFJ IP indemnity with the customary PB modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies and a 3x super-cap, plus a conforming cut to 12.1.2(f) so PB no longer covers SFJ's own infringement. We did not pursue the preferred position (narrowing PB's indemnity to PB-supplied content and PB's breach of law) because it would require striking the negotiated subject-injury and product-liability heads in Sections 12.1.2(b)-(g), a collateral rewrite.","proposal":"Add an SFJ third-party IP infringement indemnity with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x super-cap, and stop PB indemnifying SFJ for SFJ's own infringement.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-4d95b0af","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION","rationale":"The Trial Data Package is defined as all Information generated by or on behalf of either Party in the conduct of the Clinical Trials, including the Clinical Trial Database and the Research Results (p0227), so Section 11.1.1.4 vests ownership of PB-generated trial data and work product in SFJ. PB recovers ownership only on payment of the Approval Payments plus a further purchase price, and the Article 14 assignment (p0783) is expressly effective only \"in accordance with Section 11.1.1.4\", so there is no present vesting in PB. PB also has no interim licence, and SFJ's ownership carries an unrestricted right to exploit that data: Section 11.1.1.6 limits only PB-Controlled IP that PB delivers or discloses to SFJ and does not reach the SFJ-owned Trial Data Package. The clause therefore fails the fallback on both the licence-back and the service-limited-use elements. Elsewhere Article 11 is favourable (mutual retention of pre-existing IP at p0650, PB ownership of Trial Inventions and Background Materials), so we propose the fallback cure rather than reversing ownership, which would require rewriting the purchase mechanic and its cross-references in Articles 6 and 14.","proposal":"Add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to PB over the Trial Data Package and limit SFJ's use of that data to performing this Agreement.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-61a09de1","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 15.3.2 If to SFJ:","rationale":"Section 15.11 (p0833) is the only limitation-of-liability provision: it contains a mutual indirect/consequential damages waiver (which already meets that element) but no aggregate monetary cap and no carve-out architecture. Article 12 (indemnification), the 13.6 disclaimer and 14.4.2 (which only channels SFJ's termination damages into the Section 14.2 payments) add no cap, and document-wide searches for \\\"aggregate liability\\\" and \\\"shall not exceed\\\" return nothing responsive, so both Parties' direct liability is unlimited and the rule fails. We cure at preferred with two surgical operations: a single mutual cap sentence at the greater of the fees paid or payable by PB under this Agreement in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000 (Agreement-wide base, not confined to Article 6, and the floor keeps the cap meaningful given that PB's payments are event-driven), carrying the seven uncapped carve-outs; and an in-place extension of the retained savings sentence making it mutual, so that neither Party's payment obligations — including SFJ's Article 4 Development Cost funding and the Section 14.2 amounts — are \\\"damages\\\" subject to the cap. Confidentiality is tied to \\\"this Agreement\\\" to avoid any dangling cross-reference; every other word of 15.11 survives verbatim.","proposal":"Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by PB under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and a mutual confirmation that payment obligations are not capped damages","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-assign-adbfb2f5","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 15.3.2 If to SFJ:","rationale":"Section 15.6 already gives PB the preferred assignment freedom (affiliate and successor/M&A transfers without consent), but the bargain fails the playbook on three points, one of which is walk-away territory. Section 14.2.6 lets SFJ terminate the entire Agreement in its sole discretion following a PB Change of Control (with a 150% Development Costs payment), which is an express vendor exit right on our change of control. Section 15.6 also extends the same consent-free affiliate/successor carve-out to SFJ, and states no reasonableness standard for consent to other assignments; the bar on SFJ assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor expires at Program Transfer. We therefore target the preferred position: the carve-out is limited to PB, consent is subject to a reasonableness standard, the competitor bar applies at all times (waivable only in PB's sole discretion), and SFJ's change-of-control termination right is replaced with an express no-termination statement. The redline makes the shortest edits to fix duration and add the unsolicited-approach carve-out, leaving the mutual, involvement-limited, solicitation-only structure intact.","proposal":"Cap the non-solicit at 12 months after the individual's involvement ends and add an unsolicited-approach carve-out.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-4a513466","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 14.1 is the only term provision, and it sets a finite, event-based term: the Agreement expires on the earlier of termination under Section 14.2 or payment of the last Approval Payment. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — SFJ Development Funding Agreement (Execution Version)

**Prepared for:** Client (PB, the Customer party)  
**Scope:** Verified playbook findings only. No section reference or conclusion beyond the supplied findings.

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **18 findings**: 6 compliant, 10 deviations requiring redlines, and 2 items flagged **needs_review** where our automated verification did not pass and manual attorney review is required before we send comments.

The commercial architecture is unusually favourable to us on intellectual property and restraints — we retain ownership of Existing PB Intellectual Property, Trial Inventions and the Research Results, we carry no non-compete, no MFN, no counterparty audit right and no auto-renewal, and the only exclusivity covenant runs against SFJ. We are not proposing redlines in those areas; opening them would only weaken bargains that benefit us.

The exposure is concentrated in four places. First, **there is no third-party IP indemnity from SFJ anywhere in the Agreement, while Section 12.1.2(f) makes us indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by either Party** — a one-way IP indemnity running to the counterparty, which is our walk-away position. Second, **ownership of the Trial Data Package vests in SFJ** with no interim licence back to us and no use restriction on SFJ. Third, **the Section 14.2 termination formulas (300% and 150% of Development Costs, and Development Costs plus 25% per annum on a JSC disagreement) are liquidated amounts payable by us** and sit at or beyond walk-away territory. Fourth, **SFJ can terminate the entire Agreement in its sole discretion on our Change of Control** (Section 14.2.6), an express vendor exit right on our change of control.

Two further items are material but unresolved on verification: the Agreement has **no aggregate liability cap for either Party** (Section 15.11 waives indirect damages only), and our only at-will exit (Section 14.2.2) is gated on $60 million of Development Costs, closes on first Regulatory Approval and leaves the notice period blank.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (12.1.1, 12.1.2(f)) | No SFJ third-party IP indemnity; we indemnify SFJ for either Party's infringement. Add SFJ IP indemnity with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and 3x super-cap; cut 12.1.2(f) so we no longer cover SFJ's own infringement. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | Intellectual Property and PII (11.1.1.4, 11.1.1.6, Art. 14) | Trial Data Package vests in SFJ with no interim licence to us and no use limit. Add perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to PB and limit SFJ's use to performing the Agreement. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Needs review** *(verification failed)* | § 15.11 (per finding, cited at § 15.3.2 ref) | Mutual indirect-damages waiver only; no aggregate cap and no carve-out architecture, so direct liability is unlimited both ways. Proposed mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees paid/payable by PB and USD 1,000,000, with seven uncapped carve-outs and a mutual confirmation that payment obligations are not capped damages. **Attorney review required before issuing.** |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 15.6; § 14.2.6 | SFJ may terminate at its sole discretion on our Change of Control (150% Development Costs). Limit the affiliate/successor carve-out to PB, add a reasonableness standard to consent, make the competitor bar permanent, and remove SFJ's Change of Control termination right. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.4.2; 14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7, 14.2.8.1, 14.2.10) | Section 14.2 sums are payable by us "in lieu of any claim for damages" at punitive multiples. Amend the exclusive-remedy proviso to cap the payment at three months of Development Costs as the sole amount payable, whether as liquidated damages or as Trial Data Package consideration. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** *(verification failed)* | Term and Termination (14.2.2) | Our only at-will exit is gated on $60m of Development Costs, closes on first Regulatory Approval, and the notice figure is blank. Proposed unconditional 30-day convenience right with pro rata refund of prepayments and no SFJ convenience right during the Term. **Attorney review required before issuing.** |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 3.19 (with § 1.1.68) | Only exclusivity covenant runs against SFJ and its Affiliates; we have no sourcing or sole-supplier obligation. Meets preferred. No redline. |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | Art. 11 (11.1.1.1(a), 11.1.1.3, 11.1.1.4); §§ 15.6, 15.15 | No vendor-to-customer licence to police; we hold ownership, which is broader than the preferred licence position. No redline. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 3.19; Art. 7 (7.5.1–7.5.7); § 15.15 | The competing-product covenant binds SFJ, not us; Article 7 restraints are financing and licensing-consent covenants, not a non-compete. Meets preferred. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | §§ 15.9, 15.10.1, 15.10.2.2 | Delaware law is at our accepted fallback and is untouched; mandatory ICDR arbitration and delegation of scope fail the fallback. Submit unresolved Disputes to exclusive Delaware state/federal jurisdiction and confine the ICDR process to arbitrations the Parties agree to in writing. |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | Development Costs (§ 4.2.3(ii); § 6.2) | The $110m funding floor operates as a multi-year minimum draw, with no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right and no shortfall true-up. Delete the floor, leaving the election capped at $120m. |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation | Deviation | § 15.16 | Mutual and involvement-limited (good), but duration runs for the Term plus a redacted tail and there is no unsolicited-approach carve-out. Cap at 12 months after the individual's involvement ends and add the carve-out. |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Deviation | §§ 14.3, 10.3 | Section 14.3 does not apply on expiration, and the assistance and delivery periods are redacted. Insert a short free-standing Section 14.5 carrying only the three fallback elements. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | Art. 13 (13.1.1–13.1.2, 13.5, 13.6.2); § 2.2.2 | No SFJ conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy; § 13.6.2 disclaims all warranties outside Article 13. Insert a fallback-level SFJ warranty inside Article 13 (90-day software conformance, 30-day SFJ Services) with repair/replace or refund. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Records (Art. 9; §§ 3.5.5, 3.6.1, 3.6.2, 3.18.2) | SFJ holds no audit or verification right against us; the "audit" provisions are self-audit and quality-oversight mechanics. Better than preferred. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | Security Interest (§ 7.5, incl. 7.5.5) | No MFN construct binding us; the subordination covenant is a lender-protection baseline and § 7.5.5 is a consent right. Meets preferred. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal | Compliant | § 14.1 | Finite, event-based term; no renewal mechanic and no renewal uplift. At or above preferred. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (§ 12.3, 12.3.1) | Mutual programme is largely adequate, but E&O is imposed only on subcontractors (limit redacted) and there is no cyber or privacy cover. Add SFJ-only E&O USD 1m and cyber/privacy USD 2m to § 12.3.2. |

---

## Walk-away items

These three points are identified in the findings as at or beyond our walk-away position and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading material:

1. **One-way IP indemnity (Section 12.1.2(f)).** We indemnify SFJ for infringement of Third Party Intellectual Property "by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder", while SFJ gives us no IP indemnity at all. An IP indemnity running to the counterparty for the counterparty's own infringement is our walk-away position.
2. **SFJ's termination right on our Change of Control (Section 14.2.6).** An express vendor exit right on our change of control, exercisable in SFJ's sole discretion, is walk-away territory. The associated 150% Development Costs payment falls away with it.
3. **The Section 14.2 termination formulas.** Amounts payable by us of 300% of Development Costs (breach, at-will exit, bankruptcy, safety), 150% (Change of Control, compliance breach) and Development Costs plus 25% per annum where SFJ merely disagrees with a JSC decision are punitive rather than compensatory and sit at or beyond walk-away, and far outside the fallback ceiling.

---

## Next steps

1. **Clear the two needs_review items before we circulate comments.** Our proposed language for the liability cap (LOL-CAP) and the convenience termination right (T4C) did not pass verification. Both require attorney review of the drafting and cross-references — in particular the cap's interaction with Article 12, the Section 13.6 disclaimer and Section 14.4.2, and the new convenience sentence's interaction with the retained 300% Development Cost consideration under Section 11.1.1.4.
2. **Re-check the three repaired redlines.** The IP licence-back, the assignment package (including removal of the 14.2.6 consequences and confirmation that no other provision cross-references Section 14.2.6), the liquidated damages proviso and the governing law edits were repaired during drafting and should be read once more in situ.
3. **Confirm the redacted figures with the business team.** Several fallback assessments turn on bracketed redactions we cannot verify: the Section 14.2.2 notice period, the Section 15.16 non-solicit tail, the Section 14.3.3/14.3.4 transition periods, the subcontractor E&O limit, and the SFJ Interim Management Fee.
4. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the three walk-away items and the missing liability cap; carry the IP licence-back, the $110m funding floor and the arbitration-to-Delaware-courts change as primary asks; hold warranty, transition, non-solicit and insurance as the closing package.
5. **Do not open the compliant items.** Exclusivity, licence scope, non-compete, audit, MFN and renewal all sit at or above our preferred position; raising them risks inviting reciprocal drafting that reduces our current advantage.
"}

# Issues Memo — SFJ Development Funding Agreement (Execution Version)

**Prepared for:** Client (PB, the Customer party)  
**Scope:** Verified playbook findings only. No section reference or conclusion beyond the supplied findings.

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **18 findings**: 6 compliant, 10 deviations requiring redlines, and 2 items flagged **needs_review** where our automated verification did not pass and manual attorney review is required before we send comments.

The commercial architecture is unusually favourable to us on intellectual property and restraints — we retain ownership of Existing PB Intellectual Property, Trial Inventions and the Research Results, we carry no non-compete, no MFN, no counterparty audit right and no auto-renewal, and the only exclusivity covenant runs against SFJ. We are not proposing redlines in those areas; opening them would only weaken bargains that benefit us.

The exposure is concentrated in four places. First, **there is no third-party IP indemnity from SFJ anywhere in the Agreement, while Section 12.1.2(f) makes us indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by either Party** — a one-way IP indemnity running to the counterparty, which is our walk-away position. Second, **ownership of the Trial Data Package vests in SFJ** with no interim licence back to us and no use restriction on SFJ. Third, **the Section 14.2 termination formulas (300% and 150% of Development Costs, and Development Costs plus 25% per annum on a JSC disagreement) are liquidated amounts payable by us** and sit at or beyond walk-away territory. Fourth, **SFJ can terminate the entire Agreement in its sole discretion on our Change of Control** (Section 14.2.6), an express vendor exit right on our change of control.

Two further items are material but unresolved on verification: the Agreement has **no aggregate liability cap for either Party** (Section 15.11 waives indirect damages only), and our only at-will exit (Section 14.2.2) is gated on $60 million of Development Costs, closes on first Regulatory Approval and leaves the notice period blank.

## Walk-away items

These three points are identified in the findings as at or beyond our walk-away position and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading material:

1. **One-way IP indemnity (Section 12.1.2(f)).** We indemnify SFJ for infringement of Third Party Intellectual Property "by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder", while SFJ gives us no IP indemnity at all. An IP indemnity running to the counterparty for the counterparty's own infringement is our walk-away position.
2. **SFJ's termination right on our Change of Control (Section 14.2.6).** An express vendor exit right on our change of control, exercisable in SFJ's sole discretion, is walk-away territory. The associated 150% Development Costs payment falls away with it.
3. **The Section 14.2 termination formulas.** Amounts payable by us of 300% of Development Costs (breach, at-will exit, bankruptcy, safety), 150% (Change of Control, compliance breach) and Development Costs plus 25% per annum where SFJ merely disagrees with a JSC decision are punitive rather than compensatory and sit at or beyond walk-away, and far outside the fallback ceiling.

## Next steps

1. **Clear the two needs_review items before we circulate comments.** Our proposed language for the liability cap (LOL-CAP) and the convenience termination right (T4C) did not pass verification. Both require attorney review of the drafting and cross-references — in particular the cap's interaction with Article 12, the Section 13.6 disclaimer and Section 14.4.2, and the new convenience sentence's interaction with the retained 300% Development Cost consideration under Section 11.1.1.4.
2. **Re-check the three repaired redlines.** The IP licence-back, the assignment package (including removal of the 14.2.6 consequences and confirmation that no other provision cross-references Section 14.2.6), the liquidated damages proviso and the governing law edits were repaired during drafting and should be read once more in situ.
3. **Confirm the redacted figures with the business team.** Several fallback assessments turn on bracketed redactions we cannot verify: the Section 14.2.2 notice period, the Section 15.16 non-solicit tail, the Section 14.3.3/14.3.4 transition periods, the subcontractor E&O limit, and the SFJ Interim Management Fee.
4. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the three walk-away items and the missing liability cap; carry the IP licence-back, the $110m funding floor and the arbitration-to-Delaware-courts change as primary asks; hold warranty, transition, non-solicit and insurance as the closing package.
5. **Do not open the compliant items.** Exclusivity, licence scope, non-compete, audit, MFN and renewal all sit at or above our preferred position; raising them risks inviting reciprocal drafting that reduces our current advantage.
